images.title: Two trapeziums make a parallelogram
images.purpose: Shows two copies of a trapezium joined into a parallelogram of base a + b.
images.composition: One parallelogram, large and centred, made of two coloured trapeziums.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. Use coordinates in units. Trapezium 1, filled teal (#0072B2): corners (0,0), (11,0), (9,6), (2,6), so its bottom is 11 and its top is 7. Trapezium 2, the same trapezium turned half a turn, filled amber (#E69F00): corners (11,0), (18,0), (20,6), (9,6), so its bottom is 7 and its top is 11. They share the slanting edge from (11,0) to (9,6), drawn thick dark. Together they form a parallelogram with corners (0,0), (18,0), (20,6), (2,6). A grey (#6B7280) dashed vertical height from (2,6) down to (2,0) with a right angle mark. Labels: 11 cm under the teal bottom; 7 cm under the amber bottom; 7 cm above the teal top; 11 cm above the amber top; 6 cm beside the dashed height; a brace under the whole bottom with 18 cm; below that 18 × 6 = 108 and Half: 54 cm². Check: 7 + 11 = 18, 18 × 6 = 108, 108 ÷ 2 = 54.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Two copies make a parallelogram with base a + b, so one trapezium is half of it.
images.description: Shows two copies of a trapezium joined into a parallelogram of base a + b.
images.context: Matches the worked example: parallel sides 7 cm and 11 cm, height 6 cm, area 54 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Point to the bottom: the long side of one copy runs straight into the short side of the other.

image_decisions.why: The two copy construction is a single picture argument; seeing a + b along the base is the idea.
